sections.h2: Where is Logan, Utah, and what is the land like?
sections.html:
Logan is the county seat of Cache County, about 47 miles north of Ogden and 82 miles north of Salt Lake City. It sits on the Logan River near the eastern edge of Cache Valley, on the western slopes of the Bear River Mountains.

The elevation is about 4,534 feet, and Mount Logan rises to 9,710 feet to the east. Streets on the east side climb across terraces called benches, which are old Lake Bonneville sediment that the river cut through after the lake drained roughly 14,500 years ago. West of town the ground flattens into farmland and marsh, and newer subdivisions have been spreading north and south.

Where a house sits on that terrain shapes what an inspector looks at. Lots on the benches face slope and runoff questions, and lots in the flat west sit closer to farmland and marsh.

sections.h2: What are winters like in Logan, and what do they do to a house?
sections.html:
Logan has a humid continental climate with warm, usually dry summers and cold winters that bring moderate snow. Annual precipitation averages about 18.97 inches and snowfall about 61.5 inches. The record low is minus 25 degrees and the record high is 103.

Roofs carry snow load for months, and pipes in vacant houses can freeze. Winter temperature inversions can trap cold air and pollutants in the valley. An owner who cannot heat or check on a vacant house through the cold months may prefer to close before winter.

sections.h2: How did Logan become the center of Cache Valley?
sections.html:
Brigham Young sent settlers in 1859 to survey a fort site near the Logan River, and the town was named for Ephraim Logan, an early fur trapper. Logan was incorporated on January 17, 1866, and Alvin Crockett was elected its first mayor on March 5, 1866.

  • 1883: the Cache County Historic Courthouse was built.
  • 1884: the Logan Utah Temple was completed.
  • 1888: the Agricultural College of Utah was chartered, and it opened on September 2, 1890.

That college is now Utah State University. Cache County itself covers 1,173 square miles and borders Idaho, and Logan became its county seat in 1857. The county leads Utah in dairy products and is a major producer of hay, alfalfa and grain.

The 2020 census counted 52,778 people in Logan, up from 48,174 in 2010. The Census Bureau estimates 55,576 as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 median age was 24.2 and the city is home to Utah State University.

Utah State University and Space Dynamics Laboratory, a USU-owned aerospace and government contractor, are the largest employers in Logan. The university's main campus covers roughly 600 acres at the mouth of Logan Canyon.

Other employers named in reference sources include ICON Health and Fitness, Campbell Scientific, Logan Regional Hospital, JBS USA, Schreiber Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Gossner Foods, Thermo Fisher Scientific and the Cache County and Logan City school districts.

Reference sources describe the local economy as built on education, manufacturing and processing, medical services, agriculture and retail. A seller with a rental near campus should keep the academic calendar in mind when picking a closing date.

sections.h2: Which school districts and transit options serve Logan?
sections.html:
Logan City School District operates eight public schools: six elementary schools, one middle school and Logan High School. The Cache County School District serves some Logan neighborhoods as well. Charter options include Edith Bowen Laboratory School on the USU campus, Bear River Charter School, Fast Forward Charter High School and InTech Collegiate Academy.

Bridgerland Technical College offers certificate programs. Connect Transit is a sales tax funded, zero fare bus system with 15 routes serving Logan, North Logan and River Heights, and Logan-Cache Airport handles general aviation.

Confirm the school boundary for the specific address, because Logan City and Cache County districts both reach into some areas.

sections.h2: Do landlords need a license to rent out a house in Logan?
sections.html:
Yes. Logan requires every owner of a rental unit to hold a landlord business license, and each ownership entity such as an LLC, trust or corporation needs its own. An owner-occupied home that is rented only during a hospital or nursing home stay, or a temporary absence of three years or less, is the stated exception.

  • Occupancy is generally capped at three unrelated people, or one family plus one additional person.
  • Campus Residential zones allow up to six unrelated people, with no more than two per bedroom.
  • Landlords must give tenants notice of those limits in the lease or on a zoning occupancy disclosure form.
  • A lease or the form must be provided within seven days when a code official or police officer asks.

Rentals must also follow the city's Fit Premise Ordinance in Municipal Code Chapter 15.25. Units that were not legally created may need to apply for grandfathered status. A landlord selling a rental near campus should check that the license and occupancy paperwork is current, because a buyer investor will ask. Changes to ownership or agent contact information require an amendment form through the city's business licensing office.

sections.h2: How do Cache County property tax dates work for a Logan sale?
sections.html:
Cache County follows a simple calendar: valuation notices go out in July, appeals run from August to September, tax notices arrive in October and taxes are due by November 30. Current-year taxes become delinquent in December.

Delinquent taxes from the previous year are posted in January, and the Treasurer collects them or notifies new owners by the end of that month. A seller with unpaid taxes can expect the title company to pay them from proceeds at closing.

Utah also gives a 45 percent exemption on the market value of a primary home, with a 183 consecutive day residency test. New owners file Form TC-473A by September 15 after a sale, and counties cannot accept late filings. That rule applies to Logan buyers the same way it applies elsewhere in the state.

Recording is handled by the Cache County Recorder, which reports that county recording fees rose by $5 on May 6, 2026 under HB-38. The page applies to documents, subdivision plats and redactions.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Logan house work?
sections.html:
A Logan cash sale is a regular real estate closing without a mortgage lender in the middle. The buyer reviews the property, makes an offer, and a title company handles liens, taxes and the deed.

  • Describe the house and any tenants or lease dates.
  • Review the offer and the closing date.
  • Close with a title company and have the deed recorded in Cache County.

Owners of a rental with a lease running to a set date, heirs handling a house from afar and owners who do not want to pay for repairs are the sellers who most often look at this route. A buyer who takes a house with tenants in place can ask for the lease and the occupancy disclosure form described above.

faqs.q: How many people live in Logan, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 55,576 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 52,778.

faqs.q: Do I need a landlord license to rent a house in Logan?
faqs.a: Yes. Logan requires a landlord business license for every owner of a rental unit, with a narrow exception for a temporary absence of three years or less. Call 435-716-9230 for fees and renewal.

faqs.q: When are Cache County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by November 30. The Treasurer mails tax notices in October, and unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent in December.

faqs.q: How many unrelated people can live in a Logan house?
faqs.a: Generally three unrelated people, or one family plus one more person. Campus Residential zones allow up to six, with no more than two per bedroom.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Logan?
faqs.a: Utah State University and its Space Dynamics Laboratory are listed as the largest employers in Logan.
